title: Technology is changing more than the interface
lead: Three updates highlight visual experience, model availability, and users' everyday choices.
intro: Reading stories together makes patterns easier to see. This brief revisits events from June 2025 as a layout and content example; it is not a live news feed.

items.title: Apple · Liquid Glass
items.lead: A new visual material connects interfaces across platforms.
paragraphs: On June 9, 2025, Apple introduced the translucent Liquid Glass material and extended its new design to iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, watchOS 26, and tvOS 26.

items.title: Google · Gemini 2.5
items.lead: Stable releases and a lightweight preview address different needs.
paragraphs: On June 17, 2025, Google announced general availability of Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash, alongside a Flash-Lite preview. These are distinct release stages and should not be described as identical.

items.title: Firefox · 140
items.lead: More everyday operations can be left to the user.
paragraphs: Firefox 140, released on June 24, 2025, supports custom search engines, unloading tabs from the tab context menu, and resizing the pinned section of vertical tabs.

sections.title: II. Reading them together
paragraphs: Editorial observation: interfaces, models, and browsers are different product layers, but one question connects this reading: how do they change the relationship between users and tools? This is an editorial perspective, not an announced shared strategy.

conclusion.title: Keep one clear thread
paragraphs: A brief does not need to repeat every detail. State what happened and when, then leave a source the reader can check and a question worth pursuing.

footerNote: Prepared on 2026-10-13 as a retrospective of June 2025 events. Text is a short summary of the linked official sources. Metrics describe this example, not market statistics.
